says: Under a type: title, typeOnly refuses only calls and five node kinds, so a body that assigns (`expectTypeOf(n = 2)`), updates (`n++`), deletes (`delete o.a`), spreads an iterable, stringifies through a template argument, or calls a test parameter named expectTypeOf passes, though each runs code at run time; the README and plan name only getters, iterators and template strings as known gaps.
proof: In a scratch git checkout under next/, `node oxlint-plugins/lint.ts next/s` on 26719df3d with `it("type: e02", () => { expectTypeOf(n = 2).toBeNumber(); })`, `expectTypeOf(n++)`, `expectTypeOf(delete (obj as any).a)`, `expectTypeOf([...iter])` and `it("type: e05", (expectTypeOf: any) => { expectTypeOf(1).toBeNumber(); })` printed no law-shape fire for those lines, while the same file's `function f(){}` and `expectTypeOf(obj)?.toBeObject()` lines fired.
cost: A mislabeled law with a side effect or a shadowed check passes the blocking rule; adding AssignmentExpression, UpdateExpression, delete and SpreadElement to RUNS and refusing a body parameter that shadows a check name closes the cheap part.
